title: The minimum of the graph likelihood
summary: The likelihood of a finite simple undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is the probability that the uniform sequential attachment process, which at each step joins a new vertex to a uniformly random subset of uniformly random size of the vertices already present, outputs a graph isomorphic to $G$. Dervovic, Mocherla and Severini conjectured that the likelihood is minimised by the balanced complete bipartite graph. We prove that, among complete bipartite graphs of a given order, the balanced one uniquely minimises the likelihood. Exact computation shows that it also minimises over all graphs…
